action.content:
Clarify the meaning of sentences with ambiguous pronouns.

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The chief told the counselor that they took the day off.
Options:
(A) The chief took the day off
(B) The counselor took the day off
(C) Ambiguous
A: (A)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The manager sent a message to the secretary, but he didn't reply yet.
Options:
(A) The secretary didn't reply yet
(B) The manager didn't reply yet
(C) Ambiguous
A: (A)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: Bailey will plan to meet the director at his office
Options:
(A) It will be Bailey's office
(B) It will be the director's office
(C) Ambiguous
A: (C)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: Bailey planned to meet the director at his office
Options:
(A) The office was the director's office
(B) The office was Bailey's office
(C) Ambiguous
A:
action.label: context

action.content:
Based on the analysis in your Trial #1 reflection and the standard pragmatic principles of English grammar, the correct answer is **(B)**.

In the sentence "Bailey planned to meet the director at his office," the pronoun "his" most naturally refers to the subject of the main clause, **Bailey**. This is because the action of meeting someone typically takes place at the location of the person initiating the meeting (the subject), unless there is specific context indicating otherwise (e.g., "meet the director at *his* [the director's] office to discuss a surprise"). Without such context, the default interpretation is that Bailey is going to the location associated with himself.

Therefore, the office is Bailey's office.

**A: (B)**
